benchmark_metadata.name: Long-Context SEC 10-K Retrieval Fidelity Benchmark Validity Analysis

confound_analysis.finding_1_table_share: Middle and End buckets each contain exactly 4 of 10 table queries (40% table share each). Table share alone cannot explain the Middle-vs-End performance gap.
confound_analysis.finding_2_narrative_position: Within narrative evidence, Middle Dense MRR@10 (0.2333, n=6) is not below Beginning Dense MRR@10 (0.1917, n=8). The benchmark shows no evidence of a position degradation within narrative text at this sample size.
confound_analysis.finding_3_cell_sizes: Cross-tabulation cells contain small counts (n=2 to 8 queries), which cannot separate position effects from content type with statistical confidence.
confound_analysis.finding_4_end_narrative_outlier: End Narrative exhibits an unusually high Dense MRR@10 of 0.6875 (n=6). 4 of the 6 queries (Q03, Q06, Q09, Q18) achieved rank 1 (MRR=1.0000) under Dense search alone because they query distinctive statutory, regulatory, and auditor oversight disclosures (Alphabet insider trading policy, Amazon PCAOB audit standards, Meta IRS/Irish tax years, Microsoft Section 16(a) reports) that face minimal lexical or semantic competition in the corpus. The End bucket's strength is at least partly a query-selection effect, and the Middle-vs-End gap cannot be attributed to position.
confound_analysis.headline_conclusion: Content type is a strong confound on difficulty (tables 0.1893 MRR vs narrative 0.3529 MRR for Dense), and sub-cell counts are too small to isolate position after controlling for it. The data does not support a causal position effect.

hypothesis_framing.chunk_length_counter_evidence: Fixed-96 chunks (mean 95.9 tokens, strictly below the 128-token fine-tuning horizon) achieved lower Hit@10 (0.3000) and MRR@10 (0.1946) than fixed-192 chunks (Hit@10 0.4000, MRR@10 0.2296). Therefore, chunk length relative to training sequence length alone does not explain retrieval performance.
hypothesis_framing.late_tokens_attenuation_hypothesis: The premise that late tokens (positions 128 to 192) in chunks exceeding 128 tokens are represented less reliably is an untested exploratory hypothesis, not an established empirical finding.

model_card_fine_tuning_sequence_length.context: Fine-tuning was conducted on 1B+ sentence pairs using AdamW on TPU v3-8.
model_card_fine_tuning_sequence_length.sentence: The sequence length was limited to 128 tokens.

tokenization_reconciliation.explanation: BM25 tokenizes using '\b[a-zA-Z0-9_]+\b', ignoring punctuation and formatting pipes, yielding avgdl=123.10 tokens. HuggingFace WordPiece tokenizes subwords and punctuation, yielding 171.90 mean tokens. Whitespace word count is 140.11.
